relationship: For a fixed SSA setup, the sine-rule constraint can produce zero, one or two valid positions for the third vertex.

learnerLoop.action: Drag the candidate vertex along its ray and follow the sine-rule working.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The candidate triangle and side-distance test update.
learnerLoop.evidence: The construction, valid intersections and checked calculations show the number of solutions.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Decide which candidate angles form valid triangles and complete the solution set.

invariants: A valid candidate must lie on the fixed ray and at the supplied distance from the fixed vertex.
Only angle configurations that close a triangle count as solutions.
safeAdaptations: Vary SSA values that deliberately yield zero, one or two solutions.
Change working support while preserving geometric validation of each candidate.
nonGoals: Assuming every sine-rule calculation produces exactly one triangle.

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Achievement, next task or learning transition.
completion.visibility: Shown only when the local completion conditions below are satisfied; representation controls are separately identified.

completion-next.description: Advance a completed generated problem, optionally increasing Working support requirements.
completion-next.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

ssa-givens.description: One angle A and two opposite side quantities a=BC, b=AC.
ssa-givens.source: Supplied by each generated SSA problem.
ssa-givens.output: A fixes the ray; b fixes C; the circle around C has radius a.

peg-positions.description: Zero, one or two possible locations of B on the ray. These are alternatives for the SAME vertex/unknown triangle, not separate freely chosen measurements.
peg-positions.domain: Positive distance along the ray in metres.
peg-positions.source: Learner drags/releases the peg at circle/ray intersections.
peg-positions.output: Claimed triangles and measured BC are shown; a second peg gets a new cue.

candidate-angles-count.description: Sine ratio, candidate values B1/B2, their corresponding remaining C angles, and number of valid triangles. B1/B2 are possible values of angle B; count is a separate discrete conclusion.
candidate-angles-count.domain: Unitless sine ratio; angles in degrees; integer count 0, 1 or 2.
candidate-angles-count.source: Numerical inputs unlock after the construction search.
candidate-angles-count.output: The candidate table uses C=180−A−B and positive-angle validity.

modes.none: Peg every valid position (or search the ray for no solution); the numerical chain is revealed.
modes.some: Enter principal/supplementary angles where defined and final count; the no-inverse case requires the sine ratio instead.
modes.all: Also enter sine ratio and remaining candidate angles, following requiredKeys().

dependencies: For solution cases all geometry().valid peg locations must be claimed before working unlocks.
For zero-solution cases constructionReady() uses visitedMax−visitedMin >= 3.5, not a proof of an exhaustive continuous ray search.
requiredKeys() changes for no-inverse and coincident-candidate cases to avoid meaningless angle entries.
implementation.completion: solved() requires constructionReady() and workingReady(); typed values use existing ratio/angle tolerances and exact integer count.
limitations: The no-solution exploration gate measures a minimum travelled interval (3.5 model units). It must not be described as a formal exhaustive proof of no intersection.
